role: Lead Data Engineer || Lead Analytics Engineer
responsibilities: Design and develop scalable, reliable, and cost-efficient data architectures and data pipelines.
Build and maintain ETL/ELT workflows to ingest, transform, validate, and process data from multiple sources.
Develop and optimize data warehouses, data lakes, and analytical data models.
Establish data architecture standards to support growing data volumes and real-time business requirements.
Ensure data availability, consistency, accuracy, and reliability across systems.
Partner with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Business teams to identify analytical requirements and build data-driven solutions.
Develop frameworks to track product metrics, customer behaviour, user journeys, conversion funnels, retention, repeat purchases, and cohort performance.
Enable A/B testing, experimentation, feature performance analysis, and product decision-making.
Build analytical models to identify business opportunities, customer trends, operational bottlenecks, and growth drivers.
Translate complex datasets into actionable insights and recommendations for leadership.
Build and maintain dashboards, reports, and self-service analytics capabilities.
Define and standardize KPIs across product, customer experience, marketing, and operations.
Enable leadership teams to monitor business performance through reliable and timely reporting.
Improve reporting accuracy, reduce manual reporting efforts, and establish a single source of truth for key business metrics.
Establish data quality checks, monitoring mechanisms, and pipeline observability.
Define data governance practices, documentation standards, data lineage, and access controls.
Ensure appropriate handling of customer and business data in accordance with applicable privacy and security requirements.
Identify and resolve data discrepancies, pipeline failures, and performance bottlenecks.
Lead, mentor, and develop data engineers and analytics professionals.
Work closely with Product Managers, Engineering Leaders, Business Heads, and senior leadership.
Prioritize data initiatives based on business impact, technical feasibility, and organizational needs.
Drive a culture of data ownership, analytical rigor, and continuous improvement.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Ensure data availability, consistency, accuracy, and reliability across systems.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: quality, governance and observability bullets far outnumber the two speed phrases ('fast-moving', 'fast-paced product environment').
evidence.domain_risk: D2C at-home beauty and wellness services platform
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: a consumer services marketplace with no financial or regulatory reporting duties; the privacy line is generic.
evidence.collaboration_width: Product; Technology; Marketing; Operations; Finance; Business teams; senior leadership
evidence.data_team_maturity: Lead, mentor, and develop data engineers and analytics professionals.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: a data team exists to lead, but the role still has to build the platform and set standards ('build and lead our data engineering and analytics capabilities').
evidence.jd_authorship: Partner with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Business teams to identify analytical requirements and build data-driven solutions.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: bullets are generic and name no tools, volumes or methods ('build data-driven solutions').
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Develop frameworks to track product metrics, customer behaviour, user journeys, conversion funnels, retention, repeat purchases, and cohort performance.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: the main audience is product: funnels, cohorts and 'A/B testing, experimentation, feature performance analysis'.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: the role sets standards and priorities ('Establish data architecture standards', 'Prioritize data initiatives').
evidence.ai_role: Exposure to AI/ML data pipelines, feature engineering, and data infrastructure for AI applications.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: AI data infrastructure appears only as a good-to-have, not as a responsibility, so no AI skill is expected.
evidence.testing_framing: Establish data quality checks, monitoring mechanisms, and pipeline observability.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: the candidate establishes the data quality checks, an ownership framing.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Identify and resolve data discrepancies, pipeline failures, and performance bottlenecks.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: the fear is pipeline failure and data discrepancies, secondary to delivering insights.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Develop and optimize data warehouses, data lakes, and analytical data models.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: the bullets mix building new pipelines with optimising and reducing manual reporting in existing ones.
evidence.loss_aversion: Ensure data availability, consistency, accuracy, and reliability across systems. — reliability is one of several delivery goals.
